content_metadata.description: A video explaining the concept of redshift and its significance in understanding the universe.

qAndA.question: What color do light waves shift to when an object moves towards us?
How far away are astronomers able to measure the redshift of galaxies?

qAndA.answer: It provides evidence for the expansion of the universe and allows us to measure vast distances in space, looking back to its early history.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of redshift in understanding the universe?

qAndA.answer: To provide a familiar and relatable example of the Doppler Effect with sound, making it easier to understand how the same principle applies to light.
qAndA.question: Why does the video use a police car siren as an analogy for redshift?

qAndA.answer: The video begins with a curious and engaging mood, then shifts to an informative and awe-inspiring tone as it delves into the vastness and history of the universe. It ends on an appreciative note, thanking viewers for their engagement.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hello everyone and welcome to our universe. Today we will be answering the question, what
is Redshift? So this is going to be quite a quick video basically explaining what Redshift
really is. So astronomers often use the term Redshift to describe how far away objects
really are. To understand what cosmic Redshift is, we must think about sound. A great example
of this is a police car. You hear it siren because the waves travel through the air into
your ear. If the police car is moving, then the sounds in front of it are compressed and
create a higher frequency sound. And the sound waves behind it are stretched out, creating
a lower frequency sound. As the police car passes in front of you, you would hear the familiar
Doppler shift. Light is quite similar. It also travels in waves and it s quite a similar
process to what is happening within the waves. Light waves are able to be compressed and stretched,
just like sound. But with sound you would change the frequency, but with light you change the
colour. Blue light has shorter wavelengths than red. When an object in the space moves to
waters, the light waves are compressed into higher frequencies. And this is why the light
is blue shifted. It s shifted towards the shorter wavelengths. But when an object moves
away from us, the light waves are now stretched. These waves now go into the lower frequencies.
And this is what s known when the light goes to redshifted. It shifts to the longer wavelengths.
So how do we calculate distance by using redshift? Well the light from the most distant objects
in our universe is redshifted, very redshifted, as seen from earth. And this is basically
because the universe is expanding. That the further away a galaxy is, the faster it is moving.
And the faster a galaxy moves, the more its light is redshifted. So by measuring the amount
of redshift is a great way to measure the distance of a galaxy relative to earth. By using
cosmic redshift, astronomers are able to measure the distance of galaxies as far as 12 billion light
years away. With the latest technology that we have in space telescopes and ground-based
telescopes, we are pushing this cosmic redshift limit even further back, looking into the deep parts
of the universe and telling us really how the universe was created and how it evolved.
So I hope that s giving you a great insight into what is redshift. If you would like to
know any more about redshift or the expanding the universe itself, I put some links in the
description below. And as always, if you have enjoyed the video, click the like button,
and if you want to support the channel, click subscribe and support our Patreon page. Thank
you for watching and thank you for your support.
